back: About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.9% argon, 0.04% carbon dioxide, plus traces of other noble gases.

front: Boiling points of the main gases in air
Why remove CO₂ and water vapour first?
back: They would freeze into solids and block the pipes.
Compress it, remove the heat, then let it expand to cool it; repeat until it liquefies at about −200 °C.

front: Where do the gases leave the fractionating column?
back: Nitrogen at the top (lowest b.p.), argon part-way, oxygen as a liquid at the bottom.
Hospitals, welding and cutting (with ethyne), steelmaking, breathing apparatus at high altitude, and burning the fuel in rocket engines.
Haber process; liquid nitrogen for freezing food and storing semen or cells; unreactive gas in food packets.
Fire extinguishers, fizzy drinks, dry ice for refrigeration.

front: Uses of the noble gases from air
back: Argon: welding shield gas, light bulbs. Neon: advertising signs. (Helium for balloons comes mainly from natural gas.)

front: Why can air be separated by a physical method?
back: It is a mixture: its gases are not chemically combined and have different boiling points.
